definition: The tendency to feel losses more intensely than equivalent gains, often causing investors to hold losers too long or sell winners too early.
tip: Losses feel twice as painful as gains feel good. Recognize this bias when tempted to panic sell during downturns.

definition: Cash reserves covering 3-6 months of essential expenses, providing a buffer against income loss or unexpected costs.
tip: Keep in a high-yield savings account for liquidity. This isn't for investing—it's insurance against needing to sell investments at bad times.

definition: Paying off debts in order of highest interest rate first, minimizing total interest paid.
tip: Mathematically optimal. List all debts by rate, pay minimums on all, and throw every extra dollar at the highest-rate debt.

definition: When you inherit assets, the cost basis resets to the value at the original owner's death, eliminating unrealized capital gains.
tip: This makes holding appreciated assets until death extremely tax-efficient. Consider gifting assets with losses, keeping those with gains.

definition: The percentage of your income that you save and invest, the single most important variable in building wealth.
tip: A 50% savings rate means every working year funds a year of retirement. Track this number obsessively and optimize ruthlessly.

definition: Health insurance exchanges created by the Affordable Care Act where individuals can shop for coverage and access subsidies.
tip: If self-employed or early retired without employer coverage, the ACA marketplace is your primary option. Open enrollment is Nov 1 - Jan 15.

definition: The process of advocating for higher compensation during hiring or performance reviews.
tip: Research market rates on levels.fyi or Glassdoor. A single successful negotiation can be worth $100k+ over your career.

definition: Pure death benefit coverage for a specified term, providing maximum protection per premium dollar without cash value.
tip: Buy 10-15x your income for the period your dependents need protection. Term is usually 5-10x cheaper than whole life for the same coverage.

definition: The strategic distribution of investments across asset classes like stocks, bonds, and cash based on your goals, timeline, and risk tolerance.
tip: A common starting point: subtract your age from 110-120 for stock percentage. Adjust based on your risk capacity and human capital.

definition: Stock price divided by earnings per share, indicating how much investors pay for each dollar of company earnings.
tip: A P/E of 20 means you're paying $20 for $1 of earnings. Compare to historical averages and peers, but don't use in isolation.

definition: Excluding up to $250,000 ($500,000 married) of capital gains on the sale of your primary home from taxation.
tip: You must have owned and lived in the home for 2 of the past 5 years. This is one of the largest tax breaks available.

definition: Pre-tax or Roth contributions to an employer-sponsored retirement plan, reducing current taxable income or providing tax-free growth.
tip: In 2026, you can contribute up to $24,500 ($32,500 if 50+, $35,750 if 60-63). At minimum, contribute enough to get the full employer match.

definition: The age you start receiving benefits—as early as 62 (reduced) or as late as 70 (increased by delayed retirement credits).
tip: Each year you delay from 62 to 70 increases benefits roughly 7-8%. For most people, waiting until 70 maximizes lifetime benefits.

definition: Health Savings Accounts offer tax-deductible contributions, tax-free growth, and tax-free withdrawals for qualified medical expenses.
tip: In 2026, contribute $4,400 (self) or $8,750 (family). Pay medical expenses out-of-pocket now, invest the HSA, and withdraw tax-free decades later.

definition: Selling investments at a loss to offset capital gains taxes, then reinvesting in similar (but not identical) assets to maintain market exposure.
tip: Harvest losses in taxable accounts annually, but wait 31 days before repurchasing to avoid wash sale rules.

definition: Seeking information that supports your existing beliefs while ignoring contradictory evidence.
tip: Actively seek out opposing viewpoints on your investment thesis. If you can't argue the other side, you don't fully understand your position.

definition: Automatically saving and investing before paying other expenses, treating savings as a non-negotiable expense.
tip: Set up automatic transfers on payday. If you save what's left after spending, you'll save nothing. Spend what's left after saving.

definition: Paying off debts in order of smallest balance first, regardless of interest rate, for psychological quick wins.
tip: Not mathematically optimal, but the motivation from early wins helps many people stay on track. Choose the method you'll actually follow.

definition: The amount you can transfer at death without federal estate tax. In 2026, it's $15 million per person ($30 million for married couples).
tip: Most people won't owe estate tax. But state estate taxes start much lower—as low as $1 million in some states.

definition: The portfolio size needed to cover your annual expenses indefinitely, typically 25x annual spending based on the 4% rule.
tip: If you spend $60,000/year, your FIRE number is $1.5 million. Reduce spending and you lower the target while increasing savings rate.

definition: Subsidies that reduce health insurance costs for those purchasing coverage through ACA marketplaces, based on income.
tip: In 2026, the subsidy cliff returns at 400% FPL ($62,600 single). Going $1 over means losing all subsidies—manage income carefully.

definition: Restricted Stock Units are taxed as ordinary income when they vest, based on the stock price at vesting.
tip: Plan for the tax hit—vesting creates immediate income. Consider selling immediately to diversify unless you have high conviction in the company.

definition: Income replacement coverage if illness or injury prevents you from working, protecting your most valuable asset—your earning power.
tip: Aim for coverage replacing 60-70% of income. Get own-occupation coverage if possible—it pays if you can't do your specific job.

definition: Buying funds that track a market index, providing broad diversification at minimal cost without attempting to beat the market.
tip: Over 15-year periods, roughly 90% of active managers underperform their index. Keep it simple with total market index funds.

definition: A graph showing interest rates across different bond maturities, with an inverted curve historically predicting recessions.
tip: When short-term rates exceed long-term rates (inversion), it often signals economic trouble. Useful context, but don't try to time markets.

definition: Deferring capital gains taxes on investment property by reinvesting proceeds into a like-kind property within strict timelines.
tip: You have 45 days to identify and 180 days to close on replacement property. Work with a qualified intermediary—don't touch the funds.

definition: Traditional contributions reduce current taxes with taxable withdrawals; Roth contributions are after-tax but withdrawals are tax-free.
tip: If your current marginal rate is lower than your expected retirement rate, favor Roth. Most early-career workers should prioritize Roth.

definition: Benefits are reduced if you earn above certain thresholds while claiming before full retirement age.
tip: In 2026, benefits reduce $1 for every $2 earned above $24,480 if under FRA. Reductions are credited back later, not truly lost.

definition: Rather than spending HSA funds on current medical costs, invest them for long-term growth and reimburse yourself years later.
tip: Save medical receipts indefinitely. There's no deadline to reimburse yourself, so let your HSA compound for 20+ years.

definition: Strategically selling appreciated assets when your income is low enough to qualify for the 0% long-term capital gains rate.
tip: In 2026, singles can realize up to $49,450 in gains at 0% tax. Fill this bracket in low-income years or during career transitions.

definition: Overweighting recent events and extrapolating them into the future, assuming current trends will continue indefinitely.
tip: After a bull market, we expect more gains. After crashes, we expect more losses. Base decisions on long-term data, not recent returns.

definition: Allocating every dollar of income to specific categories so income minus expenses equals zero.
tip: Every dollar has a job—spending, saving, investing, or giving. Nothing is 'left over' to fritter away unconsciously.

definition: Optimizing repayment through income-driven plans, public service forgiveness, or aggressive payoff depending on your situation.
tip: If pursuing PSLF, stay on IDR plans and make 120 qualifying payments. If not, consider refinancing high-rate loans once rates drop.

definition: The amount you can give to any individual each year without gift tax implications or using your lifetime exemption.
tip: In 2026, you can give $19,000 per recipient ($38,000 from a married couple). Great for reducing your taxable estate over time.

definition: A guideline suggesting you can withdraw 4% of your portfolio in year one of retirement, adjusting for inflation, with low risk of running out over 30 years.
tip: Based on historical U.S. returns. Consider 3.25-3.5% for longer retirements, international investors, or extra safety margin.

definition: Using a High Deductible Health Plan to access HSA benefits, accepting higher out-of-pocket costs for lower premiums and tax advantages.
tip: HDHPs make sense if you're healthy and can max the HSA. The tax savings often exceed the higher deductible risk.

definition: Incentive Stock Options have favorable tax treatment if held; Non-Qualified Stock Options are taxed as ordinary income at exercise.
tip: ISOs can qualify for long-term capital gains if you hold 2 years from grant and 1 year from exercise. But watch for AMT on the spread.

definition: Excess liability coverage that kicks in after your auto and home policy limits are exhausted, protecting against catastrophic lawsuits.
tip: A $1M umbrella policy typically costs $150-300/year. Get coverage equal to your net worth plus future earnings at risk.

definition: The annual fee charged by mutual funds or ETFs, expressed as a percentage of your investment.
tip: A 1% expense ratio vs 0.03% costs you roughly 20% of your portfolio over 30 years. Choose funds with ratios under 0.20%.

definition: A measure of bond price sensitivity to interest rate changes—longer duration means higher volatility.
tip: If rates rise 1%, a bond with 10-year duration loses roughly 10%. In rising rate environments, favor shorter duration.

definition: A tax strategy for rental property owners that accelerates depreciation by classifying components into shorter-life categories.
tip: Can front-load deductions significantly. Most valuable for properties worth $500k+ and owners with high current income.

definition: Free money your employer contributes to your 401(k) based on your own contributions, typically matching 50-100% up to a percentage of salary.
tip: This is an instant 50-100% return. Never leave match money on the table—it's the highest-ROI investment decision you'll make.

definition: A spouse can claim up to 50% of the higher earner's benefit, providing a floor for couples with unequal earnings histories.
tip: The lower earner should compare their own benefit to 50% of spouse's. Often better for high earner to delay, maximizing the spousal benefit.

definition: After age 65, HSA funds can be withdrawn for any purpose (not just medical) with only income tax owed—like a traditional IRA.
tip: Max your HSA every year. Worst case, it becomes another retirement account. Best case, it covers medical costs tax-free.

definition: Concentrating itemizable expenses into a single tax year to exceed the standard deduction, then taking the standard deduction in alternate years.
tip: With the 2026 standard deduction at $16,100 (single) or $32,200 (married), bunch charitable donations and medical expenses into one year.

definition: Fixating on a specific reference point (like a purchase price or all-time high) when making decisions.
tip: Your cost basis is irrelevant to future returns. The question isn't 'Am I up or down?' but 'Is this the best use of this money today?'

definition: A budgeting framework allocating 50% of income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings and debt repayment.
tip: A useful starting point, but adjust based on your goals. FIRE pursuers might target 50% or higher savings rates.

definition: Keeping a low-rate mortgage while investing the difference rather than paying it off early.
tip: If your mortgage rate is 3% and investments return 7%, the spread builds wealth faster than prepayment. But only with money you'll actually invest.

definition: A trust you control during your lifetime that transfers assets to beneficiaries at death without probate.
tip: Avoids probate delays and keeps your affairs private, but doesn't provide tax benefits. Most valuable with real estate in multiple states.

definition: Having enough invested that compounding alone will grow your portfolio to support retirement, eliminating the need to save more.
tip: Once you hit Coast FIRE, you can take lower-paying but more fulfilling work. The math: if you have $200k at 30, it grows to $2M+ by 65.

definition: Generic drugs contain the same active ingredients as brand-name versions at a fraction of the cost.
tip: Always ask for generics when available. Use GoodRx or similar tools to compare pharmacy prices—they vary dramatically.

definition: A tax election to pay ordinary income tax on restricted stock at grant rather than vesting, potentially converting future gains to capital gains.
tip: Must file within 30 days of grant—no extensions. Valuable if you expect significant appreciation and can afford the immediate tax.

definition: Intentionally retaining risk and paying for losses out of pocket rather than purchasing insurance coverage.
tip: As your wealth grows, raise deductibles on auto and home insurance. You're essentially self-insuring smaller losses at lower premium costs.

definition: Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of market conditions, reducing the impact of volatility.
tip: Automate contributions from each paycheck. You'll buy more shares when prices are low and fewer when high.

definition: Total market value of a company's outstanding shares (share price × shares outstanding), used to categorize company size.
tip: Large-cap (>$10B), mid-cap ($2-10B), small-cap (<$2B). Smaller companies historically offer higher returns with higher volatility.

definition: When selling rental property, previously claimed depreciation is 'recaptured' and taxed at up to 25%.
tip: Depreciation isn't truly free—it's a deferral. Use 1031 exchanges to defer recapture indefinitely, or pass to heirs for step-up basis.

definition: The timeline over which you earn ownership of employer contributions to your retirement accounts.
tip: Check if your employer uses cliff vesting (all at once) or graded vesting (gradual). Factor this into job-change decisions.

definition: Bonus increases to Social Security benefits for each month you delay claiming past full retirement age, up to age 70.
tip: Benefits grow 8% per year from FRA to 70. That's a guaranteed return you can't get elsewhere—and it's inflation-adjusted.

definition: Flexible Spending Account funds typically must be used by year-end or a short grace period, or they're forfeited.
tip: Only contribute what you're confident you'll spend. Check if your plan offers a $640 rollover or 2.5-month grace period.

definition: Your marginal rate is the tax on your next dollar of income; your effective rate is total tax divided by total income.
tip: Don't fear earning more due to 'moving into a higher bracket'—only the income above the threshold is taxed at the higher rate.

definition: Continuing a behavior or investment because of previously invested resources rather than future expected value.
tip: Money already spent is gone regardless of your next decision. Ask: 'Would I buy this investment today at this price?' If no, consider selling.

definition: Designated savings buckets for irregular but predictable expenses like car repairs, vacations, or annual insurance.
tip: Create separate savings buckets for large periodic expenses. Contributes monthly so you're never caught off guard.

definition: Using credit cards strategically for rewards while paying the full balance monthly to avoid interest.
tip: 2-5% back in rewards is meaningful. Use category-specific cards for maximum returns, but never carry a balance.

definition: A trust that owns your life insurance policy, keeping the death benefit out of your taxable estate.
tip: Useful for high-net-worth individuals with estate tax exposure. You lose control of the policy but save potentially 40% in estate taxes.

definition: Having enough saved to cover most expenses, but working part-time for healthcare benefits and supplemental income.
tip: A middle ground between full FIRE and traditional retirement. Part-time work covers gaps and provides structure.

definition: A membership model where you pay a monthly fee for unlimited primary care visits, bypassing insurance for routine care.
tip: Can work well paired with a high-deductible plan for catastrophic coverage. Monthly fees typically run $50-150.

definition: The risk of having too much wealth tied to your employer's stock through equity compensation.
tip: Your job already depends on your company. Don't let your wealth depend on it too. Diversify RSUs when they vest.

definition: Choosing higher deductibles to lower premiums, effectively self-insuring smaller losses while maintaining catastrophic coverage.
tip: Insurance is for catastrophes, not minor expenses. A $1,000 deductible vs $250 can save hundreds annually in premiums.

definition: Periodically adjusting your portfolio back to target allocations by selling winners and buying underperformers.
tip: Rebalance annually or when allocations drift more than 5% from targets. Use new contributions to rebalance when possible to minimize taxes.

definition: Beta measures how much a stock moves relative to the market. Beta > 1 means more volatile; < 1 means less volatile.
tip: High-beta stocks amplify market moves both up and down. Know your holdings' beta to understand portfolio volatility.

definition: Living in a multi-unit property while renting out other units, using rental income to reduce or eliminate your housing costs.
tip: Buy a duplex, triplex, or fourplex with an owner-occupant loan (lower rates, lower down payment). Live in one unit, rent the others.

definition: A strategy where high earners contribute to a traditional IRA then immediately convert to Roth, bypassing income limits.
tip: In 2026, Roth IRA income limits start at $153k (single). If you're above this, use backdoor. But first, check for existing traditional IRA balances.

definition: Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount—higher Medicare premiums for beneficiaries with income above certain thresholds.
tip: In 2026, IRMAA kicks in at $109k (single) / $218k (married). Roth conversions in your 60s can prevent IRMAA surprises based on income from two years prior.

definition: A pre-tax account for childcare and dependent care expenses, reducing your taxable income.
tip: In 2026, the limit increased to $7,500 (up from $5,000). If you have young children in daycare, this is significant tax savings.

definition: A parallel tax system with fewer deductions that ensures high earners pay a minimum amount of tax regardless of deductions.
tip: ISOs, large state tax deductions, and certain itemized deductions can trigger AMT. Run projections before exercising incentive stock options.

definition: Following the crowd into popular investments rather than making independent decisions based on your own analysis.
tip: By the time an investment is popular, it's often overpriced. The best returns usually come from buying what others are ignoring.

definition: Setting up automatic transfers for bills, savings, and investments to remove friction and ensure consistency.
tip: Automate everything possible. 401(k) contributions, IRA transfers, bill payments. Willpower is finite; automation is not.

definition: Moving high-interest credit card debt to a 0% APR promotional card to accelerate payoff.
tip: Calculate the transfer fee (typically 3-5%) against interest savings. Have a payoff plan before the promo rate expires.

definition: Transfer on Death (brokerage) and Payable on Death (bank) designations that pass accounts directly to beneficiaries, avoiding probate.
tip: A simple way to ensure accounts transfer immediately at death. Doesn't replace a will but simplifies the process for financial accounts.

definition: Retiring early on a frugal budget, typically under $40,000/year in spending.
tip: Achievable faster but leaves little margin for error. Ensure you can sustain the lifestyle long-term, not just tolerate it temporarily.

definition: Traveling to other countries for medical procedures at significantly lower costs, especially for elective or expensive treatments.
tip: Dental work, elective surgery, and fertility treatments can cost 50-80% less abroad. Research accredited facilities carefully.

definition: Additional income from freelancing, gigs, or side businesses is subject to both income tax and self-employment tax.
tip: Side income over $400 triggers self-employment tax (15.3%). Set aside 30-40% for taxes and make quarterly estimated payments.

definition: Calculating how much coverage your dependents would need to maintain their lifestyle if you died.
tip: Factor in income replacement, debt payoff, childcare costs, and college funding. Subtract existing assets. Review every few years.

definition: Strategically locating investments across account types to minimize taxes—placing tax-inefficient assets in tax-advantaged accounts.
tip: Hold bonds and REITs in tax-advantaged accounts; keep stock index funds and international funds in taxable accounts.

definition: Risk-adjusted return metric calculated as excess return over risk-free rate divided by standard deviation.
tip: Higher Sharpe = better risk-adjusted returns. Compare funds or portfolios on a risk-adjusted basis, not just raw returns.

definition: Expenses like mortgage interest, repairs, insurance, property management, and depreciation that offset rental income.
tip: Track every expense meticulously. A rental showing paper losses can offset W-2 income if you qualify as a real estate professional.

definition: Contributing after-tax dollars to a 401(k) beyond the employee limit, then converting to Roth, potentially adding $40,000+ in Roth savings.
tip: The 2026 total 401(k) limit is $72,000. If your plan allows after-tax contributions and in-service conversions, max this out.

definition: Part A covers hospital stays (usually free), Part B covers outpatient/doctor visits, Part D covers prescriptions, Part C (Advantage) bundles them.
tip: Enroll in Part B during your initial enrollment period to avoid permanent premium penalties. Mark your 65th birthday on your calendar.

definition: A tax-advantaged savings plan for education expenses, offering tax-free growth and withdrawals for qualified costs.
tip: Contributions aren't federally deductible, but over 30 states offer state tax deductions. Check your state's plan first.

definition: Tax payments made four times per year for income not subject to withholding, such as self-employment or investment income.
tip: Pay at least 100% of last year's tax liability (110% if AGI exceeded $150k) to avoid underpayment penalties.

definition: Overestimating your ability to pick winning investments or time the market.
tip: Most professional investors underperform indexes. What makes you think you'll do better? Humility leads to better outcomes.

definition: Aligning income and expense timing to maintain positive cash flow and avoid unnecessary overdrafts or interest.
tip: Set bill due dates to align with your pay schedule. Most creditors will change due dates if you ask.

definition: Evaluating whether replacing existing debt with new debt at a lower rate makes financial sense.
tip: Calculate break-even: closing costs ÷ monthly savings = months to recoup. Only refinance if you'll stay past break-even.

definition: A legal document authorizing someone to make financial decisions on your behalf if you become incapacitated.
tip: Create a durable power of attorney before you need it. Without one, your family may need court approval to manage your affairs.

definition: Retiring early with a high spending budget, maintaining or exceeding your current lifestyle without financial constraints.
tip: Typically requires $2.5M+ portfolios. Takes longer to achieve but provides maximum flexibility and margin for unexpected expenses.

definition: Most health plans cover preventive services like annual physicals, vaccinations, and screenings at no cost.
tip: Use your free preventive benefits annually. Early detection saves lives and money. Check your plan's covered services.

definition: W-2 employees have taxes withheld and split payroll taxes with employers; 1099 contractors pay full self-employment tax and handle their own taxes.
tip: As a 1099, you pay both halves of payroll tax. Factor this in when comparing rates—you need roughly 15% more to break even.

definition: The named individuals or entities who receive your insurance proceeds, retirement accounts, and other assets at death.
tip: Beneficiary designations override your will. Review them after major life events—marriage, divorce, births, deaths.

definition: A fund tracking the entire U.S. stock market—large, mid, and small cap companies—in a single low-cost investment.
tip: A total market fund like VTI or FSKAX provides instant diversification across 3,000+ companies. This can be your entire U.S. equity allocation.

definition: A statistical measure of how two investments move relative to each other, ranging from -1 (opposite) to +1 (identical).
tip: Diversification benefits come from combining assets with low or negative correlation. Stocks and bonds typically have low correlation.

definition: Itemized deduction for interest paid on mortgage debt up to $750,000 for your primary and secondary residence.
tip: This only helps if your total itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction ($16,100 single / $32,200 married in 2026).

definition: Converting traditional IRA funds to Roth in annual installments, waiting 5 years per conversion before accessing penalty-free.
tip: Early retirees can access retirement funds before 59½ by converting during low-income years, then withdrawing conversions after 5 years.

definition: Specific periods when you can enroll in or change Medicare coverage, with penalties for missing deadlines.
tip: Your Initial Enrollment Period is 7 months around your 65th birthday. Missing it can mean 10% higher Part B premiums for life.

definition: Contributing up to 5 years of gift tax exclusions at once to a 529 plan, accelerating tax-free growth.
tip: In 2026, you can contribute $95,000 ($190,000 for couples) in one year without gift tax, treating it as spread over 5 years.

definition: Legally timing income recognition, retirement distributions, or residency changes to minimize state income taxes.
tip: If relocating from a high-tax to no-tax state, delay bonuses and Roth conversions until after establishing residency.

definition: Treating money differently based on its source or intended use, even though all dollars are fungible.
tip: A 'bonus' isn't free money to spend carelessly. Treat every dollar the same—its source doesn't change its value.

definition: Monitoring where your money goes to identify spending patterns, waste, and opportunities to optimize.
tip: Track every expense for 3 months minimum. Most people are shocked by certain categories. Awareness precedes change.

definition: Debt that finances appreciating assets or increases earning potential (good) versus debt for depreciating assets or consumption (bad).
tip: A mortgage or student loans can be good debt. Car loans and credit card debt for consumption are almost always bad debt.

definition: A legal document specifying your medical treatment preferences and designating someone to make healthcare decisions if you cannot.
tip: Also called a living will or advance directive. Every adult should have one, regardless of age or health.

definition: Moving to a lower cost-of-living area to reduce expenses, accelerating FIRE or stretching retirement savings.
tip: Your FIRE number drops dramatically in cheaper regions. Consider remote work in LCOL areas or retiring abroad.

definition: Using the 60-day election window and retroactive coverage option to minimize COBRA costs when leaving a job.
tip: Don't pay premiums unless you have a claim. You have 60 days to elect retroactively. If no claims, let it lapse and start new coverage.

definition: Negotiating separation terms when leaving a job, potentially including extended pay, benefits continuation, and favorable references.
tip: Everything is negotiable. Ask for extended health coverage, vesting acceleration, outplacement services, and a neutral reference.

definition: Temporary health insurance continuation after leaving a job, at full cost plus a 2% administrative fee.
tip: You have 60 days to elect COBRA retroactively. If healthy, wait and only elect if you have a major medical event during the gap.

definition: Allocating a portion of your portfolio to non-U.S. stocks to reduce country-specific risk and capture global growth.
tip: Consider 20-40% international allocation. Hold these in taxable accounts to claim foreign tax credits on dividends.

definition: Dollar-weighted accounts for cash flow timing; time-weighted ignores it, showing pure investment performance.
tip: Your personal return (dollar-weighted) often differs from the fund's return (time-weighted) due to when you added or withdrew money.

definition: A tax designation allowing rental losses to offset ordinary income without passive activity limitations.
tip: Requires 750+ hours and more than half your working time in real estate. Powerful for high-earning couples where one spouse qualifies.

definition: A tax-advantaged retirement account with potentially deductible contributions and tax-deferred growth until withdrawal.
tip: If covered by a workplace plan, deductibility phases out at $79,000-$89,000 (single) in 2026. Above this, use backdoor Roth instead.

definition: Up to 85% of Social Security benefits can be taxable depending on your combined income.
tip: Provisional income = AGI + half your SS benefits + tax-exempt interest. Keep it low through Roth conversions before claiming.

definition: A provision allowing unused 529 funds to roll into a beneficiary's Roth IRA, subject to annual IRA limits and a $35,000 lifetime cap.
tip: The 529 must be open 15+ years and funds must have been in the account 5+ years. A safety valve if education costs are overfunded.

definition: A charitable giving account that provides an immediate tax deduction while allowing you to distribute grants to charities over time.
tip: Contribute appreciated stock to avoid capital gains and bunch multiple years of giving into one large deduction.

definition: Preferring the current state of affairs over change, even when change would be beneficial.
tip: Review your portfolio as if building it from scratch today. Would you still buy the same things in the same proportions?

definition: A simplified approach where you automate savings first, then spend the rest guilt-free without tracking categories.
tip: If detailed budgeting doesn't work for you, just automate a high savings rate and spend the remainder freely. The key number is savings rate.

definition: Your monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income, used by lenders to assess borrowing capacity.
tip: Keep DTI below 36% for financial flexibility. Lower is better—it's also how lenders determine how much mortgage you can afford.

definition: A surviving spouse can use their deceased spouse's unused estate tax exemption by making a timely election.
tip: File an estate tax return within 9 months of death to elect portability, even if no tax is owed. This preserves up to $15 million in exemption.

definition: Systematic approaches to drawing down your portfolio in retirement, balancing longevity risk with lifestyle needs.
tip: Consider variable withdrawal rates that adjust with portfolio performance. Reduce spending in down years to preserve capital.

definition: Faith-based programs where members share medical costs, often with lower monthly costs but not technically insurance.
tip: Not regulated like insurance—pre-existing conditions may not be covered. Can work for healthy individuals, but understand the risks.

definition: The higher salary increases typically achieved by changing employers compared to internal promotions.
tip: Average raises are 3-5%. Job changes often yield 15-30%. Strategically switch employers every 2-3 years early in your career.

definition: Coverage for extended care needs like nursing homes or in-home assistance that health insurance and Medicare don't cover.
tip: Consider buying in your mid-50s when premiums are reasonable but you can still qualify. Hybrid life/LTC policies offer flexibility.

definition: The percentage of your portfolio in fixed-income securities, providing stability and income to offset stock market volatility.
tip: Bonds reduce portfolio volatility but lower expected returns. Increase bond allocation as you approach your goal date.

definition: The tendency for extreme performance to moderate over time, with outliers moving toward average results.
tip: Last year's best-performing fund is rarely next year's. Don't chase performance—high returns often revert to average.

definition: Real Estate Investment Trusts allow you to invest in real estate portfolios like stocks, without directly owning property.
tip: REITs must distribute 90% of income as dividends, which are taxed as ordinary income. Hold in tax-advantaged accounts.

definition: A retirement account funded with after-tax dollars, offering tax-free growth and tax-free qualified withdrawals after age 59½.
tip: In 2026, contribute up to $7,500 ($8,500 if 50+). The 5-year rule applies to earnings—open your Roth early to start the clock.

definition: Calculating the age at which delaying benefits pays off compared to claiming early.
tip: Break-even for claiming at 62 vs 70 is typically around age 80-82. If you expect to live beyond that, delaying wins.

definition: U.S. Treasury savings bonds with interest rates tied to inflation, providing principal protection and inflation-adjusted returns.
tip: Purchase up to $10,000/year at TreasuryDirect.gov. Current rate is 4.03%. Hold at least 5 years to avoid the 3-month interest penalty.

definition: A 20% deduction on qualified business income for pass-through entities, sole proprietors, and certain self-employment income.
tip: In 2026, the deduction phases out between $201,750-$276,750 (single). Stay below the threshold or maximize W-2 wages and property to preserve it.

definition: The tendency to sell winning investments too quickly while holding losing investments too long.
tip: Invert your instincts. Consider holding winners longer and cutting losers for tax losses. The opposite of what feels natural.

definition: Regularly reviewing recurring charges to eliminate unused or low-value subscriptions draining your accounts.
tip: Check your credit card statements for subscriptions you've forgotten. The average person wastes $200+/month on unused subscriptions.

definition: The tension between building savings and paying off expensive debt, both of which are financial priorities.
tip: Keep a small emergency buffer ($1-2k), then attack high-interest debt aggressively. Rebuild full emergency fund after debt is gone.

definition: A trust providing income to you during your lifetime, with the remainder going to charity at death, generating an immediate tax deduction.
tip: Useful for highly appreciated assets you want to sell. Avoids capital gains, provides income stream, and supports charity.

definition: A withdrawal approach with upper and lower bounds that trigger spending adjustments based on portfolio performance.
tip: If portfolio grows 20% above plan, increase spending. If it drops 20% below, cut back. Provides flexibility while maintaining safety.

definition: The most you'll pay for covered healthcare services in a plan year, after which insurance covers 100%.
tip: Once you hit this limit, all additional covered care is free that year. If facing major procedures, timing them in one year can save money.

definition: Evaluating the return on time and money spent acquiring new skills based on their impact on earning potential.
tip: High-demand technical skills can yield 50-100% salary increases. Prioritize skills with clear market value over generic credentials.

definition: Choosing the right plan by comparing premiums, deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, and expected healthcare usage.
tip: If healthy, a high-deductible plan with HSA often wins. Run the math: premium savings + HSA tax benefits vs higher potential costs.

definition: An all-in-one fund that automatically adjusts asset allocation from aggressive to conservative as you approach a target retirement year.
tip: If you want simplicity, a target date fund is a great one-fund solution. Check the glide path and expense ratio before choosing.

definition: The tendency to focus on funds or investments that survived while ignoring those that failed or closed.
tip: Fund performance data often excludes funds that were shut down for poor performance, making average returns look better than reality.

definition: Private Mortgage Insurance can be removed once you reach 20% equity in your home, eliminating the monthly premium.
tip: Request PMI cancellation at 20% equity. It's automatically removed at 22%, but why wait? You can also refinance or get a new appraisal.

definition: You have until the tax filing deadline (typically April 15) to make IRA contributions for the prior tax year.
tip: Contribute early in the year rather than waiting. A January contribution has 15 more months of tax-advantaged growth than an April contribution.

definition: A rule reducing Social Security benefits for those who receive pensions from work not covered by Social Security.
tip: If you have a government pension, your Social Security may be reduced. Factor this into retirement planning if you've worked in public sector.

definition: I Bond interest can be tax-deferred until you redeem the bond or it matures after 30 years.
tip: Unlike bank CDs, you control when to recognize I Bond income. Redeem in low-income years to minimize taxes.

definition: Taxable gains distributed by mutual funds when fund managers sell underlying securities, even if you didn't sell any shares.
tip: Check funds' distribution schedules before buying in taxable accounts late in the year—you could owe taxes on gains you didn't benefit from.

definition: Making investment decisions driven by fear of missing out on gains others are experiencing.
tip: Chasing hot stocks or crypto after big gains is reliably wealth-destroying. Stick to your plan. Boring is beautiful.

definition: Transferring your home to a trust at a discounted value, removing future appreciation from your taxable estate.
tip: You retain the right to live in the home for a set term. If you outlive the term, the home passes to heirs at the discounted gift value.

definition: Temporarily increasing bond allocation around retirement to reduce sequence of returns risk, then gradually shifting back to stocks.
tip: Peak bond allocation 5 years before through 5 years after retirement protects against early bear markets that could derail your plan.

definition: The skills, credentials, connections, and reputation you accumulate that make you valuable in the job market.
tip: Early career, optimize for learning and skill-building over salary. Career capital compounds and pays dividends for decades.

definition: Income replacement for temporary disabilities, typically covering 60% of salary for 3-6 months.
tip: Check if your employer provides STD coverage before buying your own. It bridges the gap until long-term disability kicks in.

definition: A simple, diversified portfolio consisting of just three funds: U.S. stocks, international stocks, and bonds.
tip: Example: 60% total U.S. stock, 25% total international stock, 15% total bond. Rebalance annually. That's it.

definition: Challenging your property's assessed value to potentially lower your property tax bill.
tip: Compare your assessment to recent sales of similar homes. Most appeals are free to file and successful more often than people expect.

definition: When converting IRA funds to Roth, the IRS treats all your traditional IRA balances as one pool, taxing conversions proportionally.
tip: Before backdoor Roth, roll any existing traditional IRA balances into your 401(k) to avoid unexpected taxes on conversions.

definition: Your annual statement showing estimated benefits and earnings history, available at ssa.gov.
tip: Check your statement annually for errors. Mistakes in earnings history can permanently reduce your benefits.

definition: Bonds issued by state and local governments, with interest typically exempt from federal income tax and sometimes state tax.
tip: Munis make sense in taxable accounts for high earners. Compare taxable-equivalent yield: muni yield ÷ (1 - your marginal rate).

definition: IRS rule disallowing a tax loss if you buy substantially identical securities within 30 days before or after the sale.
tip: When harvesting losses, switch to a similar but not identical fund (e.g., S&P 500 to Total Market) to stay invested.

definition: Overthinking investment decisions to the point of inaction, missing out on returns while waiting for the 'perfect' moment.
tip: A good plan executed now beats a perfect plan executed never. Start with a simple three-fund portfolio, then optimize over time.

definition: Your investment income divided by your expenses—reaching 100% means you're financially independent.
tip: Track this monthly. Watching the ratio climb from 10% to 20% to 50% is incredibly motivating.

definition: Diversifying your income sources beyond a single job to reduce risk and accelerate wealth building.
tip: Rental income, dividends, side businesses, and consulting create resilience. Start building secondary streams while employed full-time.

definition: Periodically reassessing your insurance coverage to ensure it matches your current life situation and risks.
tip: Review all policies annually. As net worth grows, you may need more umbrella coverage but can reduce life insurance.

definition: The danger that poor investment returns early in retirement will permanently impair your portfolio's longevity.
tip: Reduce stock allocation and build a cash buffer in the years before and after retirement to avoid selling stocks during a downturn.

definition: Comparing the total cost of renting versus buying, accounting for opportunity cost, maintenance, transaction costs, and appreciation.
tip: The 5% rule: if annual rent is less than 5% of the home's value, renting may be better. Run the numbers for your specific market.

definition: Moving retirement funds between accounts, with direct trustee-to-trustee transfers avoiding the 60-day indirect rollover limit.
tip: Always request a direct rollover to avoid mandatory 20% withholding and the risk of missing the 60-day deadline.

definition: Annual Cost of Living Adjustments that increase Social Security benefits based on inflation.
tip: Benefits are inflation-protected, unlike most pensions. This makes Social Security extremely valuable—factor this into claiming decisions.

definition: Short-term government securities sold at a discount and maturing at face value, with interest exempt from state and local taxes.
tip: T-bills offer competitive yields with minimal risk. In high-tax states, the state tax exemption adds meaningful extra return.

definition: An additional 3.8% tax on investment income for individuals with MAGI above $200,000 (single) or $250,000 (married).
tip: This tax applies on top of capital gains rates. Factor in the extra 3.8% when deciding between Roth conversions and taxable investing.

definition: Increasing spending proportionally with income increases, preventing wealth accumulation despite higher earnings.
tip: When you get a raise, immediately redirect at least half to savings before adjusting your lifestyle. You won't miss what you never had.

definition: Perpetually delaying retirement despite having enough, driven by fear of the unknown or desire for more cushion.
tip: If you've hit your number, the risk of regret from not retiring often exceeds the financial risk of retiring. Life is finite.

definition: Automatically using dividend payments to purchase additional shares of the same investment.
tip: Enable DRIP in tax-advantaged accounts for compounding. In taxable accounts, consider taking cash to control tax lot selection.

definition: A provision allowing you to roll funds out of your 401(k) while still employed, often to access better investment options or Roth conversions.
tip: Check if your plan allows in-service distributions for after-tax contributions—this enables the mega backdoor Roth strategy.

definition: Tax incentives for investing capital gains in designated low-income communities, including deferral and potential exclusion of gains.
tip: Complex and illiquid, but can eliminate taxes on new appreciation if held 10+ years. Only for sophisticated investors with large gains.

definition: A dollar-for-dollar credit for taxes paid to foreign governments on foreign-source income, preventing double taxation.
tip: Hold international funds in taxable accounts to claim the credit. In tax-advantaged accounts, you lose this benefit.

definition: The tendency to return to a baseline happiness level regardless of positive or negative life changes.
tip: Expensive purchases provide shorter happiness boosts than expected. Spend on experiences and relationships, not stuff.

definition: Achieving financial independence while maintaining optional income streams from passion projects or part-time work.
tip: You don't need to cover 100% with investments. A consistent $20k/year from enjoyable work reduces your FIRE number by $500k.

term: Lump Sum vs Dollar Cost Averaging
definition: Choosing between investing a windfall all at once or spreading it over time to reduce timing risk.
tip: Historically, lump sum beats DCA about two-thirds of the time. But if DCA helps you actually invest rather than wait, do that.

definition: A retirement plan for self-employed individuals with no employees, allowing both employee and employer contributions.
tip: In 2026, contribute up to $72,000 total ($24,500 employee + up to 25% of net self-employment income). Establish the plan by December 31.

definition: A tax-advantaged savings account for individuals with disabilities, allowing savings without jeopardizing government benefits.
tip: Contributions up to the annual gift exclusion ($19,000 in 2026) grow tax-free for disability-related expenses.

definition: The $10,000 limit on state and local tax deductions (property, income, sales) for federal tax purposes.
tip: If you're in a high-tax state and hitting the cap, prioritize pre-tax retirement contributions to reduce state taxable income.

definition: Overvaluing immediate rewards at the expense of long-term benefits.
tip: Automate savings and investments to remove the daily decision to prioritize your future self over present consumption.

term: Roth Conversion Ladder for Early Retirement
definition: Converting traditional IRA funds to Roth during early retirement, then accessing those conversions after 5 years.
tip: In years with no income, convert up to the top of the 12% bracket (~$50,400 in 2026). After 5 years, withdraw conversions tax and penalty-free.

definition: Tilting your portfolio toward characteristics historically associated with higher returns, such as value, small-cap, or momentum.
tip: Factor premiums exist but aren't guaranteed. If you tilt, keep it modest (10-20%) and be prepared to underperform for years.

definition: A Simplified Employee Pension allowing self-employed individuals to contribute up to 25% of net self-employment income.
tip: The 2026 limit is $72,000. SEP IRAs are simpler than Solo 401(k)s but don't allow employee contributions or Roth options.

definition: Deductions subtracted from gross income to calculate AGI, available whether you itemize or take the standard deduction.
tip: HSA contributions, student loan interest, and self-employment health insurance are above-the-line. Maximize these before chasing itemized deductions.

definition: A retirement plan for small businesses with 100 or fewer employees, with lower contribution limits but mandatory employer contributions.
tip: The 2026 employee limit is $17,000 (+$4,000 catch-up). If you have a side business, a Solo 401(k) offers more flexibility.

definition: The additional after-tax returns generated through tax-efficient investment strategies compared to a tax-unaware approach.
tip: Asset location, tax-loss harvesting, and holding period optimization can add 0.5-1% annually. Compound that over decades.

definition: Non-Roth contributions beyond the employee limit that grow tax-deferred, with earnings taxed upon withdrawal.
tip: After-tax contributions are the key to mega backdoor Roth. Convert them quickly to minimize taxable earnings in the account.

definition: Donating appreciated securities directly to charity, avoiding capital gains tax while receiving a deduction for the full market value.
tip: If you have stock with large unrealized gains, donate it instead of cash. You avoid up to 23.8% in taxes on the appreciation.

definition: Additional retirement contributions allowed for those 50 and older, increasing savings capacity in peak earning years.
tip: In 2026, add $8,000 to 401(k)s or $1,000 to IRAs if 50+. Ages 60-63 get a 'super catch-up' of $11,250 for 401(k)s.

definition: Shifting income between years or accounts to realize it in lower tax brackets over your lifetime.
tip: Convert traditional IRA funds to Roth in years when you're in the 12% or 22% bracket, before RMDs push you higher.

definition: Starting 2026, employees earning over $150,000 in FICA wages must make catch-up contributions as Roth, not pre-tax.
tip: If you earned over $150k in 2025, your 2026 catch-up contributions must be Roth. Ensure your plan offers a Roth option.

definition: A rule taxing a child's unearned income above $2,700 (2026) at the parents' marginal tax rate.
tip: Be cautious shifting investments to children's accounts. UGMA/UTMA accounts can trigger kiddie tax until age 19 (or 24 if a student).

definition: Mandatory annual withdrawals from traditional retirement accounts starting at age 73, calculated using IRS life expectancy tables.
tip: RMDs can push you into higher brackets. Consider Roth conversions in your 60s to reduce future RMD tax impact.

definition: Selecting which specific shares to sell when you've purchased the same security at different times and prices.
tip: Use specific identification to sell highest-cost lots first, minimizing capital gains. Set this as your default with your broker.

definition: Non-spouse beneficiaries must empty inherited IRAs within 10 years, with annual RMDs required if the original owner had started RMDs.
tip: Plan inherited IRA withdrawals strategically across the 10 years to avoid a large tax hit in year 10.
